title: 3D SPH Particle Fluid Simulation (Dam Break)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a 3D SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) particle fluid simulation that simulates a dam-break scenario.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[SPH Physics Model]
Particle count: N = 500 spherical particles (radius 0.08 for rendering)
Particle mass: m = 0.02 kg each
Initial distribution: uniformly arranged in a grid in the left half of the container (x ∈ [0, 2], y ∈ [0, 3], z ∈ [0, 2])

Container: rectangular cuboid 6×4×2 (x ∈ [0,6], y ∈ [0,4], z ∈ [0,2]), with only a bottom and four walls; the top is open

Core formulas:
- Smoothing kernel function (Poly6 kernel):
  W(r, h) = 315 / (64·π·h⁹) · (h²-r²)³, when r < h
  where h = 0.2 (smoothing length)

- Density calculation:
  ρᵢ = Σⱼ mⱼ · W(|rᵢ - rⱼ|, h)

- Pressure (Tait equation):
  pᵢ = k · ((ρᵢ/ρ₀)⁷ - 1)
  where k = 20.0 (stiffness coefficient), ρ₀ = 1000 (rest density)

- Pressure gradient force (Spiky kernel gradient):
  W_spiky_grad(r, h) = -45/(π·h⁶) · (h-r)² · r̂
  fᵢ_pressure = -Σⱼ mⱼ · (pᵢ+pⱼ)/(2ρⱼ) · ∇W_spiky(rᵢ-rⱼ, h)

- Viscosity force (Viscosity kernel Laplacian):
  W_visc_lap(r, h) = 45/(π·h⁶) · (h-r)
  fᵢ_viscosity = μ · Σⱼ mⱼ · (vⱼ-vᵢ)/ρⱼ · ∇²W_visc(rᵢ-rⱼ, h)
  where μ = 0.1 (viscosity coefficient)

- Gravity: fᵢ_gravity = (0, -9.81·ρᵢ, 0)

- Time integration: Semi-implicit Euler, dt = 0.001s
  vᵢ += dt · (fᵢ_pressure + fᵢ_viscosity + fᵢ_gravity) / ρᵢ
  xᵢ += dt · vᵢ

- Boundary handling: particles bounce when they collide with the container walls, with a coefficient of restitution of 0.3

Execute 3-5 physics substeps per frame to maintain stability.

[Rendering]
(1) Render particles using THREE.InstancedMesh(SphereGeometry, 500 instances)
(2) Map particle colors according to velocity: stationary = dark blue (#1a237e), fast = light blue (#42a5f5)
(3) Display the container as a wireframe
(4) Use a semi-transparent grid for the bottom surface
(5) OrbitControls

[HUD and Controls]
(6) HUD in the upper-left corner:
  - Particle count (id="particleCount")
  - Average density (id="avgDensity")
  - Average speed (id="avgSpeed")
  - Simulation time (id="simTime")

(7) Reset button (id="resetBtn"): restore the initial positions

[State Exposure]
(8) Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame with:
  - particleCount: particle count
  - particles: an array in which each item contains {x,y,z, vx,vy,vz, density, pressure}
  - avgDensity: average density
  - avgSpeed: average speed
  - maxSpeed: maximum speed
  - simTime: simulation time
  - totalKE: total kinetic energy = Σ 0.5·m·v²
  - centerOfMass: {x,y,z} center-of-mass position

Output a single standalone HTML file that runs when opened directly in a browser.
